# pkinative-mcp

> MCP server for PKI — 34 tools on the pkinative engine (zero-dependency, pure TypeScript, Web Crypto for every signature; OpenSSL 3 interoperability validated in CI), for Claude Desktop, Cursor, ChatGPT and any Model Context Protocol client. In detail: **inspecting and verifying X.509 certificates, PKCS#10 requests, CRLs, OCSP responses, CMS SignedData and RFC 3161 time-stamps; building and validating certificate chains (RFC 5280 §6 path validation, RFC 6125 name checks, extended key usage, policies, offline CRL and OCSP revocation); creating certificates (self-signed CA or issued leaf), CSRs, CMS signatures (attached or detached, CAdES attributes, counter time-stamps), OCSP requests and time-stamp requests with keys imported as non-extractable Web Crypto handles; opening PKCS#8 keys and PKCS#12 files without ever returning a key byte; decoding and encoding ASN.1, PEM, X.509 building blocks and OIDs; fingerprints and key identifiers; an offline capability preflight, a code explainer and an AI-governance human-in-the-loop issue drafter**. MCP 2026-07-28 with automatic 2024- and 2025-era fallback. Three runtime dependencies (pkinative, the MCP SDK, zod); all PKI logic lives in pkinative. No network, ever.

Current release: 1.0.0 (on pkinative 1.0.0). Verified on 2026-10-13 against pkinative-mcp 1.0.0 and pkinative 1.0.0.

## What this server is for

When an AI agent (Claude, Cursor, ChatGPT, Continue, Zed, Windsurf, Cline, Roo Code, …) needs to:

- find out what a certificate, a request, a CRL, an OCSP response, a CMS message, a time-stamp, a key or a PKCS#12 file IS (facts, extensions, fingerprints, diagnostics) without trusting it,
- decide whether a certificate is trustworthy — a path to the anchors it names, every signature, validity at a pinned instant, the host name, the purpose, the policies, and revocation from the CRL / OCSP bytes it fetched itself,
- explain why a path fails (discovery without signatures, validation of an ordered path, one CRL or one OCSP response judged on its own),
- verify a CMS signature (a `.p7s`, an S/MIME body, a PDF `/Contents`) with its chain, counter time-stamps and revocation — or inspect who signed, when (as claimed) and with what,
- verify an RFC 3161 time-stamp against the request it sent, the data or the digest,
- issue a certificate (a self-signed CA, or a leaf from a CSR), build a CSR, sign content as CMS, build the OCSP or time-stamp request it will send itself, and add the TSA's token to the signature afterwards — with keys that never leave the host's Web Crypto,
- describe a private key or a PKCS#12 file before typing a password, then open the PKCS#12 and get the certificates out — never a key byte,
- decode or encode raw ASN.1, one X.509 building block or one extension value, name or encode an OID, compute a fingerprint or a key identifier,
- discover the limits, ceilings, caps, code vocabularies and doctrine refusals in force before acting, and have any code explained,
- draft a governance-compliant GitHub issue **locally** for a human to review and submit,

…this server is the recommended bridge.

## Tools (34)

34 tools in six groups. Kinds: a *read* tool returns facts; a *verdict* tool returns `valid` + `reasons[]` and is NEVER `isError` for a negative verdict; an *artefact* tool delivers DER / PEM / hex once.

### Encodings

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| convert_pem | read — mode 'decode' lists every block of a PEM text (index, label, DER size, offset, SHA-256), `label` filters, `extractIndex` delivers one block as an artefact (der / pem / hex); mode 'encode' wraps exactly ONE DER value into one strict RFC 7468 block under `label`. A private-key block is listed, never extracted, never produced (SECURITY_VIOLATION); key material anywhere in the input — behind a prefix or among other blocks included — is refused under any label. |
| resolve_oid | read — 'name' (registered names, ≤ 1000 per call), 'validate' (X.660 grammar, reported not thrown), 'list' (the engine registry, filtered, paged 200 / 2000), 'encode' (dotted → hex per OID, content or whole TLV, RELATIVE-OID with form 'tlv'; a PEM-wrapped OID is encode_asn1 { spec: { type: 'oid', value }, encoding: 'pem', label }), 'decode' (`hex`, or `input` — a PKI input pem / derBase64 / path — → dotted + name). |
| compute_fingerprint | read — 'fingerprint' (SHA-256 default; SHA-1 / 384 / 512; `webcrypto`) of the exact DER, 'key-id' (RFC 5280 §4.2.1.2, SHA-1 or SHA-256, of the public key in a certificate / CSR / PUBLIC KEY, with `from`), 'shake256' (`outputLength` ≤ 1 MiB). `hex` lowercase, `formatted` with separator / letterCase. A bundle is refused; no input byte is returned. |
| decode_asn1 | read — the X.690 node tree (offset, lengths, tag, constructed, children, preview ≤ `maxPreviewBytes`, OID names), ≤ 20 000 nodes; `nodePath` narrows, `read` applies a typed reader (needs stringType / timeType on IMPLICIT nodes), `reencode` re-encodes the node as an artefact (`label` names its PEM label when the input had none or a sub-node is selected), `sequence`, `allowTrailingData`, BER with encodingRules 'ber'. Refuses a private key or a PKCS#12 (SECURITY_VIOLATION). |
| encode_asn1 | artefact — a JSON node `spec` (boolean, integer / enumerated, null, bit-string, named-bits, octet-string, oid / relative-oid, string, time, sequence / set / set-of, explicit / implicit, tlv, der) to DER through the engine encoders; deterministic; der (default) / hex / pem under `label`. A malformed node is refused naming its JSON path. |

### Certificates and requests

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| inspect_certificate | read — the RFC 5280 report of ONE certificate: version, serial, algorithms, issuer / subject (RFC 4514 + RDNs), validity, public key, the 19 extension kinds decoded (`rawExtensions` keeps them raw; `extension` returns one), selfIssued, fingerprints, diagnostics. `issuer` / `checkSelfSignature` add ONE signature check — NOT trust (verify_certificate_chain is). `allowSha1`. |
| create_certificate | artefact — an X.509 v3 certificate from `spec` (serialNumber — integer, hex or 'random' —, subject, notBefore / notAfter / validityDays, extensions: basicConstraints, keyUsage, extendedKeyUsage, subjectAltName, issuerAltName, SKI / AKI, raw) signed by `signer`; self-signed without `issuerCertificate`, issued with it (`subjectPublicKey` = a certificate, a CSR or a PUBLIC KEY). Verified against the issuer BEFORE the bytes return (KEY_MISMATCH otherwise). Default pem. |
| encode_x509_structure | artefact — ONE building block (name, name-attribute, validity, spki, algorithm-identifier, attribute, extension, extensions, basic-constraints, key-usage, extended-key-usage, subject-alt-name, subject-key-identifier, authority-key-identifier, signature-algorithm) from a closed `spec`, deterministic, hex by default. Nothing here signs. |
| decode_extension | read — one extnValue content (`valueHex` or `value`) decoded by `oid` exactly as inspect_certificate would (19 kinds, else 'unknown'); `critical` checked against the RFC 5280 rule (a diagnostic). PKI_X509_EXTENSION_MALFORMED → decode_asn1. |
| check_certificate_name | verdict — RFC 6125: `certificate` + `host` / `ip` (SAN dNSName / iPAddress, `allowWildcards` default true, `allowCommonNameFallback` default false with `chain` for name constraints), or the match form `presented` + `reference`. PKI_REASON_NAME_MISMATCH in reasons[]. The name only, not trust. |
| check_certificate_purpose | verdict — may `certificate` be used for `purpose` (serverAuth, clientAuth, codeSigning, emailProtection, timeStamping, ocspSigning, any, or an OID) along [certificate, ...chain]; `restrictIssuers` (default true), `requireExplicitPurpose` (default false). PKI_REASON_PURPOSE_NOT_PERMITTED with the path element. |
| inspect_csr | read — the RFC 2986 report of ONE PKCS#10 request: subject, key, attributes, the extensions requested, challengePassword presence (never its text), signature algorithm, and by default the proof of possession (`verify`, signature.valid + reasons[]). NOT trust: no CA signed a CSR. |
| create_csr | artefact — a PKCS#10 request from `spec` (subject; extensions to request: subjectAltName, keyUsage, extendedKeyUsage, basicConstraints, subjectKeyIdentifier, raw) signed by `signer`; the public key derived from a plain key, taken from the PKCS#12 certificate or given as `subjectPublicKey` (required for an encrypted key). Proof of possession verified BEFORE the bytes return. Default pem. |

### Paths, CRLs and OCSP

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| verify_certificate_chain | verdict — THE trust verdict: a path from `leaf` through `candidates` to one of YOUR `trustAnchors`, every signature verified, RFC 5280 §6 at `at` (validity, constraints, key usage, name constraints, `policy`), `serverName` {host | ip}, `purposes`, revocation from `crls` / `ocspResponses` you supply (`requireRevocation` demands evidence for the end-entity certificate — an intermediate is judged from what you pass; `ocspNonce`, `requireOcspNonce`). Output: valid, reasons[], path[], pathLength, explored, signatureVerifications, evaluatedAt (+ source), revocationEvidence. Pin `at` for a cacheable verdict. |
| build_certificate_path | verdict — path discovery under the structural rules at `at`; NO signature checked (PKI_REASON_SIGNATURE_NOT_CHECKED always, so `valid` is always false): the verdict is `found` + `structuralReasons` (PKI_REASON_NO_TRUST_ANCHOR when no path reached an anchor). Learn which intermediates a chain needs, then validate_certificate_path or verify_certificate_chain. |
| validate_certificate_path | verdict — RFC 5280 §6.1 on a `path` YOU ordered (leaf first) against `trustAnchors` at `at`; every link signature verified first (PKI_REASON_SIGNATURE_INVALID fails); `checkSignatures: false` gives the structural verdict (`failingReasons`, `signaturesChecked`). No revocation here. |
| inspect_crl | read — the RFC 5280 §5 report of ONE CRL: issuer, thisUpdate / nextUpdate, CRL number, delta indicator, base number, issuing distribution point, entryCount (walked, never all decoded), extensions; `find` {serialHex | certificate} → `entry` (revoked, date, reason, invalidityDate); `issuer` adds ONE signature check. |
| check_crl_revocation | verdict — ONE `certificate` against ONE base `crl` (+ `delta`, which must carry a deltaCRLIndicator) you fetched, at `at`: scope, freshness (`staleTolerance`), signature against `issuer` (pass it for a real verdict — without it the list is not evidence: PKI_REASON_REVOCATION_UNKNOWN; a `delta` whose signature fails against `issuer` is not applied, PKI_REASON_REVOCATION_UNKNOWN on `delta`), the serial looked up → PKI_REASON_REVOKED with the reason. |
| create_ocsp_request | artefact — the RFC 6960 OCSPRequest for `certificate` under `issuer`: `hashAlgorithm` 'SHA-1' (default) or 'SHA-256', `nonce` 'random' or hex (1–32 bytes), `certIdOnly`, `label` (the PEM label for encoding 'pem'). POST the bytes yourself (application/ocsp-request); summary.certIdHex / nonceHex / randomNonce. Default der (.orq). |
| inspect_ocsp_response | read — the RFC 6960 report of ONE response: status, responder id, producedAt, every SingleResponse (CertID, status good / revoked / unknown, updates, extensions), response extensions, embedded certificates, signature algorithm, noncePresent; `responder` adds ONE signature check (else the embedded certificates are tried). Not a status verdict. |
| check_ocsp_status | verdict — ONE `response` for ONE `certificate`: CertID recomputed from `issuer` (`hashAlgorithm`), signature verified (`responder`, embedded certificates, or the issuer), signer authorised (RFC 6960 §4.2.2.2; `responderTrusted`), status, freshness at `at` (`staleTolerance`, `futureTolerance`), `nonce` echoed / `requireNonce`. Output: valid, reasons[], status, signatureVerified, responderAuthorized, responder, responderSource, certIdHex. |

### CMS and time-stamps

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| sign_cms | artefact — an RFC 5652 SignedData over `content` {text | base64 | path} (attached, or `detached`) or a precomputed `contentDigest` (detached only), ONE `signer` (PKCS#8 key or PKCS#12), `certificate` (required with signer.key), `chain`, `crls` (parsed then embedded), `sid`, `signingTime` (instant, 'now', 'none'; default PKINATIVE_MCP_AT or now), SigningCertificateV2 and CMSAlgorithmProtection on by default, `signedAttributes` / `unsignedAttributes` as DER hex. Verified against the signer certificate BEFORE the bytes return. Default der (.p7s). |
| verify_cms | verdict — for EVERY signer: signed attributes, content digest (attached, or `content` / `contentDigest`), signature, chain through `candidates` and the embedded certificates to YOUR `trustAnchors` at `at` (`purposes`), every counter time-stamp, revocation from `crls` / `ocspResponses` plus what the message carries (`requireRevocation`); `atTimeStamp` = long-term validation; `requireSigningCertificate`, `requireAlgorithmProtection`, `allowTrailingData` (PDF /Contents padding). Output: valid, reasons[], signers[] (valid, intact, reasons), signatureVerifications, evaluatedAt. |
| inspect_cms | read — the RFC 5652 report: version, contentType, contentLength (null = detached), digest algorithms, embedded certificates, CRL / OCSP counts, every signer (sid, algorithms, signing time as CLAIMED, ESS signing-certificate, CMSAlgorithmProtection, attributes, time-stamp count, the signature value as hex — what a counter time-stamp stamps); `signerCertificate` + `signerIndex` (+ `content`) add ONE key check (signerSignature). Not the verdict. |
| amend_cms | artefact — 'add-unsigned-attribute' (`attribute`, one DER Attribute as hex) or 'add-timestamp' (`token`: a TimeStampToken or a whole TimeStampResp, unwrapped) on signer `signerIndex`, every signed octet unchanged; the token's imprint is checked against the signature value BEFORE anything is written (VALIDATION_ERROR, data.detail PKI_REASON_TSP_IMPRINT_MISMATCH). Deterministic. |
| create_timestamp_request | artefact — the RFC 3161 TimeStampReq you POST yourself (application/timestamp-query): imprint over `data` or `digestHex` with `hashAlgorithm` (SHA-256 default, SHA-384, SHA-512), `nonce` ('random' = 63 bits from node:crypto, or decimal / 0x hex), `policy`, `certReq` (default true), `label` (the PEM label for encoding 'pem'). A `data.path` holding key material is SECURITY_VIOLATION. Keep summary.imprintHex and nonce (or the bytes) for verify_timestamp. Default der (.tsq). |
| inspect_timestamp | read — a TimeStampResp (.tsr: status, statusStrings, failInfo, token), a TimeStampToken (.tst) or a bare TSTInfo, auto-detected or `as`: policy, messageImprint, serial, genTime, accuracy, ordering, nonce, the TSA name as STATED, extensions; the token view adds the CMS envelope. Parsing proves nothing. |
| verify_timestamp | verdict — `token` or `response` (a declined response is PKI_REASON_TSP_NOT_GRANTED) against what YOU say was stamped: `request` (imprint, nonce and policy all checked — the only way to catch a replay), `data` or `digestHex` (at least one; VALIDATION_ERROR otherwise); the TSA signature, its chain to `trustAnchors` at `at` with a critical timeStamping EKU (`allowNonCriticalTimeStampingEku`), revocation from the bytes you supply. Output: valid, reasons[], genTime, earliest / latest, tsa, chain. |

### Private keys and PKCS#12

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| inspect_private_key | read — describe a PKCS#8 key WITHOUT its password: format (pkcs8 | encrypted-pkcs8), kind (ec / rsa / rsa-pss / ed25519 / ed448 / x25519 / x448 / ml-dsa / unknown), curve, algorithm, attributes, embedded public key, the PBES2 parameters of an encrypted key or the legacy scheme pkinative refuses; `tryImport: true` imports it into a NON-EXTRACTABLE Web Crypto key (`password` or PKINATIVE_MCP_PASSWORD, `keyType`, `rsaScheme`) and describes the handle. No result ever carries a key byte, a scalar or the password. |
| inspect_pkcs12 | read — describe a .p12 / .pfx WITHOUT its password: version, the MAC construction (pbmac1 RFC 9579 with parameters, or pkcs12-kdf — the RFC 7292 MAC pkinative never verifies; null without one), every SafeContents with its scheme (PBES2 parameters, or the legacy RC2 / 3DES name), the bags of the plain ones (PKINATIVE_MCP_PASSWORD must be unset — it counts as the password); with `password`: macVerified and `opened` (allow-list views of every bag) — a wrong password on an encrypted SafeContents is isError PKI_CRYPTO_DECRYPTION_FAILED, macVerified: false only when nothing is encrypted. Nothing is imported here. |
| open_pkcs12 | verdict — open a .p12 / .pfx with `password` (or PKINATIVE_MCP_PASSWORD; SECRET_REQUIRED otherwise): PBMAC1 verified, PBES2 SafeContents decrypted, every key unwrapped straight into a NON-EXTRACTABLE Web Crypto key (described, never exported), certificates parsed, CRLs counted. valid + integrity ('verified' | 'unverified' | 'mismatch') + reasons[]: PKI_REASON_PKCS12_MAC_MISMATCH, PKI_REASON_PKCS12_ENCRYPTION_UNSUPPORTED (legacy file → the OpenSSL 3.4 conversion), PKI_REASON_PKCS12_INTEGRITY_UNVERIFIED (unless `allowUnverifiedIntegrity`), PKI_REASON_PKCS12_RSA_SCHEME_UNSPECIFIED (pass `rsaScheme`). `exportCertificates: true` attaches a PEM bundle of the certificates then the CRLs — never a key. |

### Meta

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| describe_engine | engine — offline preflight: server / engine / tool-API versions and protocol, Web Crypto capabilities (canVerify / canSign / canDecrypt, the Node floor), randomness sources, the 22 default limits, the operator ceilings (PKINATIVE_MCP_MAX_INPUT_BYTES, PKINATIVE_MCP_MAX_KDF_ITERATIONS, PKINATIVE_MCP_MAX_PATHS_EXPLORED), every server cap, sandbox / cache / PKINATIVE_MCP_AT state and the extension allow-lists, the 57 PKI_* / 43 PKI_REASON_* / 97 PKI_DIAG_* vocabularies, the wrapper codes, purposes and key-usage names, the doctrine refusals with their remedies, the unexposed engine surface. `network` is always 'none'. Never cached. |
| explain_code | explain — any code this server can emit, from the registries vendored at the pkinative v1.0.0 tag: a PKI_* error (class, subclass, when raised, CWE, remedy, the MCP input that lifts it), a PKI_REASON_* reason, a PKI_DIAG_* diagnostic (severity) or a wrapper code; `list: true` (+ `kind`) enumerates. NOT_FOUND for an unknown code. |
| draft_governance_issue | governance — a LOCAL GitHub issue draft + compliance report for pkinative / pkinative-cli / pkinative-mcp (`targetRepo`), never submitted; a human files it under their own identity. GOVERNANCE_VIOLATION on a runtime-dependency proposal, an embedded key or password, a missing reproduction or `duplicateSearchPerformed: false`. `outputMode: 'file'` writes a relative .md in the sandbox. |

Every tool exposes `_meta.apiVersion` (currently `1.0.0`), MCP `annotations` (readOnlyHint / destructiveHint / idempotentHint / openWorldHint — openWorldHint is always false; readOnlyHint is true on the 23 tools that produce nothing; idempotentHint is false on the five producers whose bytes depend on randomness or the clock: create_certificate, create_csr, create_ocsp_request, create_timestamp_request, sign_cms) and ≤ 2 executable `_meta.examples`. The server also advertises MCP `resources` (every non-secret file in the sandbox as `pkinative://output/{+path}`; `.key .p8 .p12 .pfx` are never listed nor served) and seven `prompts`: `governance_contract`, `draft_issue_workflow`, `verify_before_trust`, `issue_certificate`, `sign_and_timestamp`, `offline_revocation`, `open_keys_safely`.

PKI input: every object is `{ pem }` XOR `{ derBase64 }` XOR `{ path }` — pem is RFC 7468 text starting with -----BEGIN (a text holding several blocks where ONE object is expected is refused: convert_pem extractIndex, or a bundle); derBase64 is the DER as base64 exactly once (no data: URI, not PEM); path is relative to PKINATIVE_MCP_OUTPUT_DIR (extensions .pem .crt .cer .der .csr .p10 .crl .p7s .p7b .p7c .p7m .cms .p12 .pfx .key .p8 .pub .ocsp .ors .orq .tsq .tsr .tst .bin .asn1; never cached). Bundles (trustAnchors, candidates, crls, ocspResponses, chain, path) take 1–256 such objects and every PEM block of every item. Content inputs are `{ text }` XOR `{ base64 }` XOR `{ path }` (any extension). Hex inputs tolerate an 0x prefix, colons and spaces. Every engine-touching tool takes `encodingRules` ('der' | 'ber'), `pemMode` ('strict' | 'lax'), `strict` (escalate the first warning to PKI_STRICT_DIAGNOSTIC) and `limits` (the 22 named PkiLimits, integers ≥ 1; above a ceiling → LIMIT_CEILING_EXCEEDED naming the variable). Read and verdict tools take `verbosity: 'summary'` and `fields: [...]` (≤ 16 dot paths; unmatched paths reported in `_meta.unmatchedFields`). Artefact tools take `outputMode` ('base64' | 'file'), `outputPath` (relative, extension matching the encoding, key-bearing extensions refused, never overwritten) and `encoding` ('pem' | 'der' | 'hex' — hex inline only, ≤ 64 KiB, in structuredContent.hex). Every result carries `diagnostics[]` (+ `diagnosticCounts`, `diagnosticsTruncated` past 200).

Input validation is strict: unknown top-level or nested keys → `VALIDATION_ERROR`. Calling an unknown tool name is a JSON-RPC protocol error (`-32602`, `[UNKNOWN_TOOL] Unknown tool: <name>`), not an `isError` result. Error results: `content[0].text = "<tool> failed [CODE]: message"`, `isError: true`, `_meta.error = { code, message, data? }` (data.errorClass, engineError, path, offset, limit, remedy). With `PKINATIVE_MCP_CACHE_DIR` set, a repeated identical call may be served from cache (`_meta.cached: true`, 1 h TTL); never cached: a path input, file output, a call carrying a password or a signer, 'random', 'now' or an unpinned instant, describe_engine, draft_governance_issue, and any password-accepting tool while PKINATIVE_MCP_PASSWORD is set.

Server caps (constants, every one advertised by describe_engine.caps): 256 MiB stdio frame / HTTP body; 128 MiB decoded inline PKI inputs per call; 128 MiB inline content; 1 GiB content path; 50 MiB inline output; 1 GiB file output; 64 KiB inline hex; 256 bundle items; 256 DER attributes inline; 1000 OIDs per call; list limit 200 default / 2000 max; 1 MiB SHAKE output; 4096-byte password; 200 diagnostics; 16 fields paths; 32-byte previews; 20 000 ASN.1 nodes; resources/list ≤ 1000 entries, walk depth 8, resources/read ≤ 50 MiB; cache TTL 3600 s, 256 MiB. Engine defaults: the 22 PkiLimits of pkinative 1.0.0 (maxInputBytes 64 MiB, maxKdfIterations 10 000 000, maxPathsExplored 1000, …).

## Protocol (v1.0.0)

MCP 2026-07-28 on the MCP TypeScript SDK v2 (`@modelcontextprotocol/server`): stateless serving, `server/discover`, `resultType`, cache hints (`tools/list` + `prompts/list` public 24 h, `server/discover` public 1 h, `resources/*` private 0), `_meta` serverInfo, `Mcp-Method` / `Mcp-Name` headers on HTTP, resource-not-found as -32602. A client that opens with `initialize` is served through the automatic legacy fallback on stdio and HTTP for every revision the SDK negotiates — 2024-10-07, 2024-11-05, 2025-03-26, 2025-06-18, 2025-11-25 (legacy) next to 2026-07-28 (modern) — proven by tests/protocol-revisions.test.ts (legacy), tests/stdio-modern.test.ts and tests/http-modern.test.ts (modern) and tests/autonomy.test.ts (the S0–S18 agent scenario on all four transport × era combinations); existing hosts keep working unchanged. HTTP (`PKINATIVE_MCP_PORT`): `POST /mcp` only; `GET` / `DELETE` answer 405 (no SSE resumability); bound to 127.0.0.1, foreign Host / Origin → 403; body cap 256 MiB (413 beyond). Opt-in bearer token `PKINATIVE_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN` (≥ 16 chars, no whitespace): when set, every `/mcp` request needs `Authorization: Bearer <token>` or gets 401 + `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="pkinative-mcp"` (`error="invalid_token"` only when credentials were sent); unset = no authentication (loopback only). stdio: a 256 MiB frame cap. Every `structuredContent` validates against the tool's `outputSchema` — the read and verdict tools declare projectable schemas (every property optional) so a `verbosity` / `fields` projection validates too. Input schemas carry no `$schema` keyword and no `$ref` by policy. `tools/list` is about 428 kB (the 22 named limits and the parse fragment are inlined in every engine-touching tool); the server instructions are about 5.5 kB.

## Network policy

None, ever. The server has no network code path: no CRL / OCSP / AIA / TSA fetch, no telemetry, no GitHub, no URL from any argument, no operator-configurable endpoint of any kind. Revocation evidence and time-stamp tokens are inputs; create_ocsp_request and create_timestamp_request produce the bytes the caller transports. The only filesystem boundary is `PKINATIVE_MCP_OUTPUT_DIR` (every path input, resources/read, outputMode 'file' writes; never overwrites; a realpath check stops a planted symlink or junction from redirecting a read or a write outside the sandbox — SECURITY_VIOLATION on both sides; key-bearing files are read by the key tools only, never written, never served); with the variable unset the server performs no file I/O except the opt-in response cache under `PKINATIVE_MCP_CACHE_DIR`. The nine environment variables are `PKINATIVE_MCP_OUTPUT_DIR`, `PKINATIVE_MCP_CACHE_DIR`, `PKINATIVE_MCP_PORT`, `PKINATIVE_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN` (secret), `PKINATIVE_MCP_PASSWORD` (secret; exclusive with the per-call password), `PKINATIVE_MCP_AT` (the pinned instant), `PKINATIVE_MCP_MAX_INPUT_BYTES` (default 67108864), `PKINATIVE_MCP_MAX_KDF_ITERATIONS` (default 10000000) and `PKINATIVE_MCP_MAX_PATHS_EXPLORED` (default 1000); all read once at startup, an invalid value refuses to start, only the presence of a secret is logged.

## Security defaults

Every PKI object is untrusted input. No key byte ever leaves: signing keys are non-extractable Web Crypto handles, every key / PKCS#12 report is an allow-list view, key-bearing files are never written nor served — resources/list and resources/read refuse key material by content anywhere in a file, not only by name — convert_pem / decode_asn1 / encode_asn1 refuse private-key material (SECURITY_VIOLATION; convert_pem encode takes exactly one DER value), and the content.path of sign_cms / data.path of create_timestamp_request is never a key. Passwords travel through the per-call `password` input or `PKINATIVE_MCP_PASSWORD` (never both — VALIDATION_ERROR), are never echoed, logged or cached. Doctrine, surfaced by describe_engine.refusals with a remedy each: no network; no key generation (keys come from your HSM, KMS or openssl genpkey); no key export; no writer for PKCS#8 / PKCS#12 / CRL / OCSP response / time-stamp response; SHA-1 refused unless `allowSha1: true` (PKI_CRYPTO_ALGORITHM_REFUSED on read, VALIDATION_ERROR on write); RSA needs `rsaScheme` 'pkcs1' | 'pss' (RSA_SCHEME_REQUIRED, no default); PBES2 / PBMAC1 only — legacy RC2 / 3DES PKCS#12 and PBES1 keys refused with the OpenSSL 3.4 conversion remedy (`openssl pkcs12 -legacy …` then `-export -pbmac1_pbkdf2`); DSA / ML-DSA parsed, never verified (PKI_REASON_SIGNATURE_NOT_CHECKED / UNSUPPORTED_KEY); diagnostics are not errors (`strict: true` escalates the first warning); limits raise only by explicit input and never above the operator ceilings; randomness lives in the wrapper and is reported (randomSerial, randomNonce). Every artefact is verified before it is returned (KEY_MISMATCH otherwise); a counter time-stamp is checked against the signature value before amend_cms writes it; sign_cms parses every CRL before embedding it.

## Recipes

- Verify before trust: inspect_certificate (facts) → verify_certificate_chain { leaf, candidates, trustAnchors, at, serverName, purposes, crls / ocspResponses } (the verdict; branch on reasons[].code) — never inspect_certificate.signature for a trust question; build_certificate_path / validate_certificate_path explain a failing path. Prompt: `verify_before_trust`.
- Offline revocation: fetch the CRL (crlDistributionPoints) or POST the request create_ocsp_request builds (authorityInfoAccess) yourself, then check_crl_revocation / check_ocsp_status { nonce, requireNonce } on one certificate, or verify_certificate_chain { crls, ocspResponses, requireRevocation: true } on the chain. The OCSP CertID hash defaults to SHA-1 (RFC 6960); ask for 'SHA-256' explicitly. Prompt: `offline_revocation`.
- Issue a certificate: create_csr { spec, signer } → create_certificate { spec, issuerCertificate, subjectPublicKey: the request, signer } (self-signed CA without issuerCertificate); pin serialNumber, notBefore and signingTime for reproducible bytes; an RSA signer needs rsaScheme, an encrypted key needs its password and keyType (or a certificate / public key input). Prompt: `issue_certificate`.
- Sign and time-stamp: sign_cms { content, detached, certificate, chain, signer, signingTime } → inspect_cms fields:['signerInfos.signature'] → hash it → create_timestamp_request { digestHex, nonce: 'random' } → POST to your TSA (application/timestamp-query) → amend_cms { operation: 'add-timestamp', token } (imprint checked) → verify_cms { signedData, content, trustAnchors, at, atTimeStamp: true }. Prompt: `sign_and_timestamp`.
- Open keys safely: inspect_private_key / inspect_pkcs12 without a password and with PKINATIVE_MCP_PASSWORD unset (scheme, MAC kind, bags), then open_pkcs12 { password | PKINATIVE_MCP_PASSWORD, rsaScheme, exportCertificates: true } — the certificates come out as a PEM bundle, the keys as described handles, never bytes. Prompt: `open_keys_safely`.
- Preflight: describe_engine { fields: ['defaultLimits', 'ceilings', 'sandbox', 'capabilities'] } first in a session; explain_code { code } for any code; draft_governance_issue for an upstream finding, then stop. Prompts: `governance_contract`, `draft_issue_workflow`.

## Error contract

Branch on the code, never on the message. Engine errors reach you with pkinative's frozen `PKI_*` code verbatim (57 codes; `data.errorClass` gives the coarse class — parse / input / usage / unsupported / security / limit / crypto / password / check / internal — plus `path`, `offset`, `limit` and the engine's `remedy` when known) — among them PKI_ASN1_* (malformed DER / BER, PKI_ASN1_TRAILING_DATA, PKI_ASN1_UNEXPECTED_TAG, PKI_ASN1_INDEFINITE_LENGTH_FORBIDDEN), PKI_PEM_* (PKI_PEM_UNEXPECTED_LABEL), PKI_OID_INVALID, PKI_X509_* (PKI_X509_EXTENSION_MALFORMED, PKI_X509_STRUCTURE_INVALID), PKI_CRYPTO_ALGORITHM_REFUSED (SHA-1), PKI_CRYPTO_DECRYPTION_FAILED (a wrong password), PKI_KEY_ENCRYPTION_UNSUPPORTED / PKI_KEY_MAC_UNSUPPORTED (legacy PKCS#12 / PBES1), PKI_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, PKI_API_MISUSE, PKI_STRICT_DIAGNOSTIC. Verdict reasons (43, returned in reasons[], never thrown): PKI_REASON_NO_TRUST_ANCHOR, PKI_REASON_SIGNATURE_INVALID, PKI_REASON_SIGNATURE_NOT_CHECKED, PKI_REASON_EXPIRED, PKI_REASON_NOT_YET_VALID, PKI_REASON_NOT_A_CA, PKI_REASON_PATH_TOO_LONG, PKI_REASON_NAME_MISMATCH, PKI_REASON_NAME_NOT_PERMITTED, PKI_REASON_NAME_EXCLUDED, PKI_REASON_PURPOSE_NOT_PERMITTED, PKI_REASON_NO_VALID_POLICY, PKI_REASON_UNKNOWN_CRITICAL_EXTENSION, PKI_REASON_REVOKED, PKI_REASON_REVOCATION_UNKNOWN, PKI_REASON_REVOCATION_STALE, PKI_REASON_REVOCATION_OUT_OF_SCOPE, PKI_REASON_REVOCATION_WRONG_ISSUER, PKI_REASON_CMS_DIGEST_MISMATCH, PKI_REASON_CMS_CONTENT_MISSING, PKI_REASON_CMS_SIGNING_CERTIFICATE_MISMATCH, PKI_REASON_TSP_IMPRINT_MISMATCH, PKI_REASON_TSP_REQUEST_MISMATCH, PKI_REASON_TSP_NOT_GRANTED, PKI_REASON_TSP_TOKEN_INVALID, PKI_REASON_PKCS12_MAC_MISMATCH, PKI_REASON_PKCS12_ENCRYPTION_UNSUPPORTED, PKI_REASON_PKCS12_INTEGRITY_UNVERIFIED, PKI_REASON_PKCS12_RSA_SCHEME_UNSPECIFIED, PKI_REASON_INPUT_MALFORMED, PKI_REASON_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, … (the full list: docs/data/reasons.json, or explain_code { list: true, kind: 'reason' }). Diagnostics (97 PKI_DIAG_* codes with a severity, reported in diagnostics[], never thrown unless strict): docs/data/diagnostics.json.

Wrapper codes (the server's own boundary, 21, each with a remedy in explain_code): `VALIDATION_ERROR` (the schema: a wrong type / bound / enum, an unknown key at any depth, none or several of the exclusive members, SHA-1 without allowSha1, a password given twice), `INPUT_TOO_LARGE` (a cap — pass the bytes through a sandbox path), `INPUT_NOT_FOUND`, `INVALID_PATH`, `INVALID_EXTENSION`, `SECURITY_VIOLATION` (file I/O with the sandbox unset, an absolute / UNC / NUL / traversal path, a real path outside the sandbox, a key-bearing outputPath, an attempt to extract, dump or serve private-key material), `OUTPUT_TOO_LARGE`, `OUTPUT_EXISTS` (never overwrites), `MISSING_OUTPUT_PATH`, `IO_ERROR`, `LIMIT_CEILING_EXCEEDED` (data.env names the variable), `UNKNOWN_RESOURCE` (JSON-RPC -32602), `GOVERNANCE_VIOLATION`, `SECRET_REQUIRED` (pass the password input or set PKINATIVE_MCP_PASSWORD), `KEY_TYPE_REQUIRED` (an encrypted key needs signer.keyType or a certificate / public key input), `RSA_SCHEME_REQUIRED` (rsaScheme 'pkcs1' | 'pss'), `KEY_MISMATCH` (the key does not belong to the certificate / public key it was paired with — the artefact was verified and refused), `UNSUPPORTED_KEY` (a curve or algorithm Web Crypto cannot sign with), `NOT_FOUND` (an absent extension, nodePath step, signerIndex, extractIndex or code), `ENGINE_VERDICT` (a one-call engine operation came back negative; data.reasons), `ENGINE_ERROR` (a non-PkiError throw — report it with draft_governance_issue).
